response.content:
## Defence and Drone Companies Entering the Norwegian Market in 2026

Norway's defence and drone sector saw significant activity in 2026, driven by a defence budget exceeding €10 billion and a national drone strategy launched in late 2025. Here are the key companies and initiatives that entered or expanded in the Norwegian market during 2026:

### Ukrainian Drone Producers (via "Build with Ukraine" initiative)
- In January 2026, Ukraine's Defence Minister Denys Shmyhal and Norway's Defence Minister Tore Sandvik signed an agreement to jointly produce Ukrainian combat drones on Norwegian soil. A pilot production line was established in Norway, with the first deliveries of several thousand medium-range strike drones expected by summer 2026. Norway fully financed the project with additional funding on top of its $7 billion defence aid commitment to Ukraine.
- In April 2026, Prime Minister Støre and President Zelenskyy signed a broader defence declaration in Oslo expanding drone production cooperation, with Ukraine sharing battlefield data and technical expertise while Norway provided industrial capacity and R&D partnerships with Norwegian research institutions.

### Robot Aviation AS (Norwegian, expanding)
- Norwegian company Robot Aviation, which builds Arctic-ready long-endurance drones for Norway's military, grew from 5 to nearly 60 employees since 2023 and expanded significantly in 2026, aiming to be "as far as possible" independent of international suppliers.

### Stendr (Norwegian AI drone defence startup)
- Norway-based Stendr raised $5.4 million in funding for its AI-native drone defence systems, building a vertically integrated hardware and software stack for the defence sector.

### OSL Technology (Terma subsidiary, Denmark/UK)
- OSL Technology, a UK-based subsidiary of Danish defence group Terma, was selected as one of five companies on NATO's new Counter-UAS marketplace (launched November 2026). OSL's systems already protect two Norwegian military air bases.

### Kongsberg Maritime (Norwegian, new capability)
- Kongsberg Maritime launched the unmanned vessel **Arctic Hunter**, developed as part of the UK's Type 92 programme for submarine detection in the High North.

### Arondite (UK defence tech)
- UK-based Arondite deployed its **Cobalt** mission orchestration software with the UK Commando Force and announced plans to make the platform available to Norwegian units for joint testing under the JEF Northern Navies Initiative signed in Oslo in November 2026.

### Latvian Drone Companies
- A Latvia–Norway Drone Forum was held in Oslo in March 2026, bringing together Latvian drone technology and autonomous systems companies to explore partnerships with Norwegian defence firms, investors, and government representatives.

### German Defence Companies
- A dedicated workshop ("Doing Defence Business in Norway – Tips & Pitfalls") was organised in 2026 specifically for German defence companies looking to enter or expand in Norway, following a German-Norwegian Defence Dialogue. The focus included M&A as a route to market entry.

### Broader Context
- The Nordic countries (Norway, Sweden, Denmark, Finland, Iceland) announced in November 2026 that they would work towards a common defence deal to boost NATO's overall capabilities.
- Norway's Long-Term Defence Plan commits to increasing total defence spending by more than €50 billion by 2036, with substantial investments in drone technologies and autonomous systems — creating ongoing opportunities for international companies entering the market.

# UK to buy three new mine-hunting drone motherships under Norway agreement

The decision, for which £90 million ($119.1 million) has been allocated, was formalized on Thursday by British Defense Secretary Wes Streeting and his Norwegian counterpart, Tore O. Sandvik, at the Atlantic Future Forum in Oslo.

By Elisabeth Gosselin-Malo  on November 13, 2026 9:16 am

Share Options

Share a link to this article

 Email
 Facebook
 LinkedIn
 X

 

The UK will buy three counter-mine "motherships" from Norway under a new agreement. (UK Ministry of Defence) [...] MILAN — The UK this week formalized plans to purchase three new mine-hunting “motherships” that can deploy unmanned mine countermeasure assets, as part of a defense cooperation agreement with Norway.

Under the UK-Norway Lunna House Agreement, signed last December, the British government announced its intention to join the Norwegian P1118 Standardized Vessel Program to develop offshore support vessels as motherships for autonomous mine-hunting systems.

The decision, for which £90 million ($119.1 million) has been allocated, was formalized on Thursday by British Defense Secretary Wes Streeting and his Norwegian counterpart, Tore O. Sandvik, at the Atlantic Future Forum in Oslo. [...] “This deal strengthens our ability to protect freedom of navigation, which is critical to our security and our economy…[We are] using the biggest sustained increase in defense spending since the Cold War to put the latest modern technology in the hands of our sailors,” Streeting said.

The British Ministry of Defense said the vessels, built on the same family as Norway’s naval version of the P1118 design, will help keep sailors “further from danger” and, as a result, support “anti-submarine warfare capabilities on NATO’s northern flank.”

The first ship is expected to arrive in 2031, and the deal includes an option for London to order three more.

“The Cobalt mission orchestration software will enable seamless co-ordination between UKCF, UK defense units and partner forces across the JEF coalition. It will also allow future hardware and AI capabilities to be deployed rapidly,” reads the release.
